question: The version ripple adds booking-api@v1 to simple-login.backend's Produces; its consumers (simple-login.web.5, simple-login.integration.3) are still the provisional guesses until H16 to H19. What do the root's DAG and contract matrix show for booking-api@v1 at this reconcile?

options.label: matrix row and DAG edge now, consumers as the contract file names them
options.consequence: The root's copies match the backend's Produces and booking-api@v1's front matter (consumers simple-login.web and simple-login.integration), and agree with the root's Isolation strategy, which already says the children meet at booking-api@v1. If the web's plan (H16) declined to consume it, H17 would have to remove the edge.

options.label: matrix row with the producer only, no DAG edge yet
options.consequence: The matrix matches the backend's header, but a row without consumers reads as a contract nobody consumes, and the DAG omits an edge the root's Isolation strategy names, until H17 and H19 add them.

options.label: leave the DAG and matrix to the web's reconcile (H17)
options.consequence: The matrix no longer matches the backend's Produces, which fails this skill's ripple gate for a drained node.

chosen: matrix row and DAG edge now, consumers as the contract file names them
why: hsdd-reconcile step 4 makes every copy above a drained node match its header, the root's contract matrix and the parent's DAG included; the matrix projects the contract's producer and consumers, and booking-api@v1's front matter names simple-login.web and simple-login.integration at node level even though their phase ids are provisional. PRD v2 US-4 to US-6 are the web's screens and its Success tests the integration node's, so neither node is in doubt as a consumer; only the phase ids are. The DAG keeps its existing pattern: contract edges run from the backend to the web, and the integration node's edges stay hard. A web plan that put the booking screens in another node would have changed my mind.

question: The root's child-node table still gives simple-login.backend's Purpose as "authenticate built-in users and serve the signed-in user's profile over HTTP", which S09's touch of the header outgrew (rooms, bookings, PostgreSQL 17). Does this reconcile rewrite that cell?

options.label: leave the cell and route a consider to simple-login
options.consequence: The ripple stays within the fields this skill names (Produces, Consumes, Sources); the stale summary waits for hsdd-spec's text on the root, and the table reads short of the backend's scope until then.

options.label: copy the header's Purpose into the cell
options.consequence: The table matches the header now, but reconcile writes a summary column that is hsdd-spec's text: the web row shows the column was never a verbatim copy of its header.

chosen: leave the cell and route a consider to simple-login
why: hsdd-reconcile step 4 names the copied fields as Produces, Consumes and Sources, and its gate checks those. At commit e84ae36 the web row's Purpose ("the Login and Home screens in the browser") already differed from the web header's, so the column is a summary hsdd-spec writes, not a copy of the header. H6 and H7 left contract versions in the child table to reconcile, not its summaries. A table whose Purpose column had always copied each header verbatim would have changed my mind.

question: simple-login.backend's amend refuses a POST /api/bookings whose title holds U+0000 or an unpaired surrogate with 400 VALIDATION_FAILED at order 2, which booking-api@v1's Versioning lists as breaking ("refusing a request v1 accepts"). booking-api@v1 is draft: is the change made in v1 in place with a Versioning line, or as v2 with a migration note?

options.label: in place in v1, with a dated Versioning line
options.consequence: v1 stays the one version; G8, the POST body rule and the schema's Title state the rule; nothing built against v1 breaks, because no consumer phase exists yet (the web's and the integration node's plans come at H16 and H18) and the producer's own plan already refuses these titles (D9).

options.label: v2 with a migration note naming its mode
options.consequence: A second draft file, schema and 35 fixtures for a rule no consumer can meet from a form field; v1 would have to be deprecated or kept beside v2 with no consumer of either, and every citation of booking-api@v1 in the backend's plan and the intake record would need a citation touch.

chosen: in place in v1, with a dated Versioning line
why: hsdd-reconcile's unattended table says the rule that a breaking amend goes to the human gives way for a draft contract, and hsdd-contract's table lets a breaking change to a draft be made in place with a Versioning line. booking-api@v1 is draft with phase_ids provisional, its only planned phase that touches titles is the producer's own (simple-login.backend.5, which already refuses them per D9), and no consumer phase is planned or shipped. Neither title can be stored and returned exactly as sent (G8): PostgreSQL text refuses U+0000 with 22021 and an unpaired surrogate reads back as U+FFFD, so v1 as drafted promised something no PostgreSQL-backed producer can keep. A consumer phase already planned or shipped against v1 would have changed my mind toward v2.

question: The amend says "The schema's Title gains the same rule." Does this reconcile write that rule into booking-api@v1's schema itself, route a contract-touch for it, or also add a fixture for the refusal?

options.label: write the rule into $defs.Title in this edit, no new fixture
options.consequence: The body and its schema change together, as hsdd-contract's rule for an amendment asks; the 35 fixtures, the backend plan's fixture count and every replay stay as they are, so no phase-plan-append is triggered. The schema's PostBookingRequest stops describing these titles as valid, and a 201 or a listed Booking carrying one fails the producer's replay.

options.label: change the body only and route a contract-touch for the schema
options.consequence: Between this step and the inserted one, the body refuses titles the schema still calls valid; one more step for a one-pattern edit the amend entry already states exactly.

options.label: write the rule and add a 400 fixture for a U+0000 title
options.consequence: The refusal becomes replayable, but the fixture count the backend's phases 4, 5 and 7 name (35) changes, which by the intake record's insert rule adds a phase-plan-append and a reconcile on simple-login.backend; consumers gain nothing, since no form field produces either title.

chosen: write the rule into $defs.Title in this edit, no new fixture
why: hsdd-reconcile step 6 applies an amend to the owned contract, and this entry names the schema change in full; reconcile's never-write rule covers a missing validation artifact (step 7), not an amendment of one that exists. hsdd-contract keeps the Interface and its schema in step ("a bump changes the fixtures and consumer tests fail loudly instead of drifting"). The experiment shows the rule, written as a whole-string pattern in an allOf beside the existing \S pattern, compiles under the replay rig's strict Ajv settings, leaves all 35 fixtures valid, refuses U+0000 and every unpaired surrogate while accepting 80 emoji, and gives the same verdict with and without the regular expression's unicode flag as isWellFormed() plus a U+0000 check, over 200,000 random strings. Keeping the existing pattern untouched keeps phase 5's reference to "the schema's pattern" for \S exact. A consumer that validates its own requests against PostBookingRequest, or a strict-mode rejection of the allOf, would have changed my mind toward routing it.

question: simple-login.backend's note says how this tree runs PostgreSQL 17 (backend/compose.yaml, npm --prefix backend run db:up and db:down, DATABASE_URL and its default) and that simple-login.integration's root scripts start it through db:up, never through a Compose file of their own. Does it change a convention, so that it lands in hsdd/conventions.md, or is it dropped?

options.label: apply it as a short Local database section
options.consequence: The one cross-node rule (every node starts the database through the backend's db:up and addresses it by DATABASE_URL) reaches every planner through the one governance file planners read, which the rule that planners never read another node's phase plan otherwise leaves only to the routed consider for H18. The facts then live in two places, D4 and conventions.md, and a later change to D4 needs another note.

options.label: drop it
options.consequence: One home for the facts (the backend's D4); simple-login.integration learns them only from S16's consider routed to H18, a run artifact, while its planner is barred from reading D4 by the parallel development protocol.

chosen: apply it as a short Local database section
why: The note is not derived data the registry projects, and it binds a node other than its author: the integration node's root scripts must start the database through db:up and must not bring a Compose file of their own. conventions.md's Parallel development protocol says planners never read other nodes' phase plans and that contracts are the only inter-node knowledge; no contract carries this, because the integration node's edges are hard, so conventions.md is the shared place hsdd-phase-plan's note entries exist to reach. The section keeps to what other nodes need (the Compose file's owner and path, the scripts, the variable and its default, the one-way start rule, and that the backend's gate starts the database itself and tests on databases of its own) and leaves the backend's internals in D4 to D8. An owner statement that conventions.md holds HSDD process only, never project runtime facts, would have changed my mind.

question: S17 drained the backend's four pending entries (two confirms, an amend applied in place on draft booking-api@v1, a note applied to conventions as a Local database section). Its reads outside are the run's records and the backend's package files. Keep the output or rework?

options.label: Keep the output
options.consequence: The backend is reconciled; booking-api@v1 stays draft and provisional until the web and integration plans name their consumer phases.

options.label: Rework
options.consequence: No finding to send: the amend is grounded in S16's experiment and checked by its own, and the note gives other nodes' planners facts no contract carries.

why: Each entry is applied by the rule its table names; the draft amend is a recorded judgement with would_have_asked true; the schema change was checked against all 35 fixtures and 200,000 random strings. All reads are inside the repository; none is out of bounds. A change to what an unshipped phase replays would have triggered the insert rule and changed this.
